claims.text: A CALPHAD-based high-throughput design strategy will yield HEAs with improved phase stability, refined microstructure, and enhanced properties compared with traditional experimental design.
As-cast or solidified HEAs generally exhibit mixed phases and conventional microstructural inhomogeneity.
CALPHAD-based high-throughput computation can screen and tune HEA compositions.
The screening and optimization process uses thermodynamic parameters to select compositions.
CALPHAD high-throughput screening requires adequate computational software and database resources.
Composition ranges and temperature profiles are relevant controlled variables in high-throughput HEA design.
The design strategy will produce a refined microstructure dominated by a single-phase solid solution.
The design strategy will reduce undesired secondary and intermetallic phases.
CALPHAD calculates mixing enthalpy, entropy, and atomic-size differences as key screening parameters.
CALPHAD enables rapid screening of large HEA composition spaces.
CALPHAD screening identifies compositions that favor phase stability and homogeneous microstructures.
Favoring phase stability and homogeneous microstructures optimizes mechanical and physical properties.
CALPHAD-designed HEAs will show statistically significant improvements in phase purity, microstructure refinement, strength, and ductility over trial-and-error-designed alloys.
HEAs designed without computational optimization typically exhibit multiple phases, microstructural inhomogeneity, and suboptimal mechanical properties.
Expected benefits are limited to HEA systems within validated compositional and processing ranges.
The approach may not translate directly to alloys with fundamentally different chemistries or processing routes.
The magnitude of improvements remains uncertain until experimentally validated and may vary by alloy system and processing parameters.
XRD, SEM/TEM, and mechanical testing can compare phase composition, microstructure, strength, hardness, and ductility between CALPHAD-designed and traditionally designed HEAs.
